stem: Buyer preview: SaaS · 22 FTE · €18K/mo spend, heavy on AWS · just closed Series-B €15M. Which archetype?
feedback_correct: A Series B, heavy AWS spend, 22 FTE and a founder-CEO: that is Tom's profile. Open with a signal that has a number in it.
feedback_incorrect: A recent funding round, card spend driven by engineering, a small team and SaaS add up to Tom's profile. Maria, Emma and Lukas have no recent funding signal.

stem: You're calling Lukas: a German restaurant group with 4 locations. His top objection is 'I don't trust new fintechs.' Which prop do you lead with?

options.text: Prop 2: multi-user cards with per-card limits
Prop 3: auto-FX at the interbank rate
Prop 4: receipt capture and accounting sync

feedback_correct: Lukas wants to cap what each of his 4 site managers can spend. Multi-user cards with per-card limits (Prop 2) do that, with real-time spend control (Prop 1) in support. You build trust by showing control, not by pitching FX.
feedback_incorrect: Lukas's main pain is controlling spend across 4 sites, so Prop 2 (a card with its own limit for each site manager) leads. Prop 3 (FX) only comes in later, for his payments to the Italian supplier.

stem: You ran M1, M2 and M3 cleanly with Maria (UK retail). You ran them the same way with Lukas (German restaurants), but the call ended cold. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: Lukas needs an opener built on a number, not on behaviour, and you didn't switch styles.
You should have pitched Prop 4 instead of Prop 1.
M3 calendar close doesn't work in German.

feedback_correct: UK buyers respond to openers about behaviour ('who approves what'). German buyers respond to signals with numbers in them (FX volume, headcount, monthly spend), as L.D. found. The moves stay the same, and the framing follows the buyer.
feedback_incorrect: M1, M2 and M3 work the same for every buyer type. What changes is how you frame the diagnostic: behaviour for UK buyers, numbers for German buyers.

stem: You score a new lead: industry fit 4, FTE band 4, monthly spend 3, decision-maker access 4, intent signal 3. What do you do?

options.text: Dial first and score it after the call

feedback_correct: 4 + 4 + 3 + 4 + 3 makes 18. That is the bottom of the 18 to 21 band, so the lead goes on this week's list. Only 22 or more gets a call today.
feedback_incorrect: Add the five scores: 4 + 4 + 3 + 4 + 3 = 18. Below 18 means skip, 18 to 21 means dial this week, and 22 or more means dial today. This lead goes on this week's list.
